c005.front: In what order do the logical operators work?
c005.back: First NOT, then AND, OR last. Comparisons (=, >, LIKE…) are evaluated even earlier. a OR b AND c means a OR (b AND c). When in doubt, add parentheses.

c006.front: Where do NULLs go by default when sorting?
c006.back: Oracle treats NULL as the largest value. With ASC the NULLs come last, with DESC first. You can change this: NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST.

c007.front: What does the row-limiting clause look like (since 12c)?
c007.back: ORDER BY ... OFFSET n ROWS FETCH {FIRST|NEXT} m [PERCENT] ROWS {ONLY|WITH TIES}. OFFSET skips n rows, FETCH takes the next m. WITH TIES needs ORDER BY.

c008.front: How do you search for a real % or _ with LIKE?
c008.back: Declare an escape character with ESCAPE: name LIKE '%\_%' ESCAPE '\'. Then \_ means an ordinary underscore, not "any single character".

c009.front: & vs && in substitution variables: what is the difference?
c009.back: &var asks for a value at every use (unless the variable is already defined) and does not remember it. &&var asks once and keeps the value until the end of the session (or until UNDEFINE). SET VERIFY ON shows the old/new lines.

c010.front: What is x BETWEEN a AND b equal to?
c010.back: x >= a AND x <= b. Both limits are included. If a > b (for example BETWEEN 10 AND 5), nothing matches.

c106.front: Why do you write '&name' for text, not &name?
c106.back: SQL*Plus only pastes the text in before sending the statement. Without the quotes King becomes a column name and you get ORA-00904. Numbers need no quotes.
c106.try_sql:
-- This is the statement after substituting &name without quotes
SELECT last_name FROM employees WHERE last_name = King;

c107.front: How do you stop SQL*Plus from prompting for a value at the & in 'R&D'?
c107.back: SET DEFINE OFF (turn it back on with SET DEFINE ON). SET VERIFY OFF does not help: it only hides the old/new lines.

c108.front: DEFINE, DEFINE x, DEFINE x = v, UNDEFINE x: what do they do?
c108.back: DEFINE shows all variables. DEFINE x shows one. DEFINE x = v creates a CHAR variable that is used without prompting. UNDEFINE x removes it, so &x prompts again.

c109.front: What does SET VERIFY ON / OFF do?
c109.back: ON (the default): SQL*Plus prints old N: and new N: lines, that is, each line with a variable before and after substitution. OFF hides them, but substitution still works.

c110.front: What can ORDER BY refer to?
c110.back: A column (even one not selected), an expression, an alias or a position number in the SELECT list. With DISTINCT or set operators (UNION…) only to what is in the SELECT list (otherwise ORA-01791). A bad position number: ORA-01785.

c111.front: What does col NOT IN (1, 2, NULL) return?
c111.back: No rows. It means col <> 1 AND col <> 2 AND col <> NULL, and the last test always gives UNKNOWN. IN (1, 2, NULL) works normally.

c1100.back: Error ORA-01722. ||, + and - have the same precedence and work from left to right, so 'Total: 10' is built first and then 'Total: 10' + 5 fails. Write 'Total: ' || (10 + 5). On the other hand, 5 + 10 || ' total' gives 15 total.

c1101.front: What is NOT (a OR b) equal to? And NOT (a AND b)?
c1101.back: NOT (a OR b) = NOT a AND NOT b. NOT (a AND b) = NOT a OR NOT b (De Morgan's laws). NOT without parentheses negates only the nearest condition.

c1102.front: FETCH FIRST 2.7 ROWS ONLY, FETCH FIRST 0 ROWS ONLY, OFFSET 20 ROWS with 9 rows?
c1102.back: 2 rows (the fraction is truncated), 0 rows, 0 rows. None of them raises an error.

c1103.front: How many rows does FETCH FIRST n PERCENT ROWS return?
c1103.back: CEIL(n / 100 * number of rows), that is, rounded up. Example: 25 PERCENT of 9 rows is 2.25, so you get 3. WITH TIES may add rows tied with the last one.

c1104.front: In what order do you write ORDER BY, OFFSET and FETCH?
c1104.back: ORDER BY ... OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY. FETCH before OFFSET raises ORA-00933 (ORA-03049 in 23ai). Oracle has no LIMIT.

c1105.front: What does WHERE ROWNUM <= 3 ORDER BY salary return?
c1105.back: Three arbitrary rows, sorted only afterwards: ROWNUM is assigned before ORDER BY. Sort in a subquery and filter ROWNUM outside, or use ORDER BY ... FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY.

c1106.front: Does NULL match NOT BETWEEN 20 AND 30?
c1106.back: No. NOT BETWEEN is col < 20 OR col > 30, and for NULL the result is UNKNOWN. A row with NULL drops out with BETWEEN, NOT BETWEEN, IN and NOT IN.

c1107.front: An undefined &id appears twice in one statement. How many times does SQL*Plus prompt?
c1107.back: Twice, and you can give different values. &&id (or an earlier DEFINE id) prompts once and uses that value everywhere.

c1108.front: After DEFINE pre = emp, what does FROM &pre.loyees become?
c1108.back: FROM employees. The period ends the variable name and disappears. If you want a real period after a variable, write two: ..

c1109.front: What does DEFINE job = Sales Rep store?
c1109.back: Only Sales (DEFINE JOB = "Sales" (CHAR)). An unquoted value ends at the first space. Write DEFINE job = 'Sales Rep'.

c1110.front: dept is defined; SET DEFINE OFF; then &dept is used. What happens?
c1110.back: &dept is not substituted and the statement fails (SP2-0552). The variable still exists: after SET DEFINE ON, &dept turns into its value again without prompting.

c1111.back: Banana, apple, cherry. A binary sort puts all uppercase letters before lowercase ones. To sort regardless of case, use ORDER BY UPPER(w).
